extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) handling applications with unavailable or non-joining inventors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for filing and processing patent applications when one or more inventors refuse to join, cannot be found, are deceased, or otherwise unavailable, including substitute statements, petitions, proof of proprietary interest, and examiner handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventors must apply jointly and make required oaths/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint inventors must apply for a patent jointly, and each joint inventor must make the inventor's oath or declaration required by 37 CFR 1.63, except as provided for in 37 CFR 1.64. (See 35 U.S.C. 116.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a joint inventor refuses to join in an application for patent or cannot be found or reached after diligent effort, the other joint inventor(s) may make the application for patent on behalf of themselves and the omitted inventor; 37 CFR 1.45(a) cross-references 37 CFR 1.64 concerning execution of a substitute statement by the other joint inventor(s) in lieu of an oath or declaration. See MPEP § 604 for additional information pertaining to substitute statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy when joint inventor refuses or cannot be found
rubrics_metrics.description: When a joint inventor refuses to join in an application for patent or cannot be found or reached after diligent effort, the application may be made by the other inventor(s) on behalf of the nonsigning inventor (pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 116 and 37 CFR 1.47).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such filings under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47 require a petition including proof of the pertinent facts, payment of the fee set forth in § 1.17(g), and the last known address of the nonsigning inventor. See MPEP §§ 409.03(d)–(g) for proof requirements and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47(a) filing requirements (at least one joint inventor available)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47(a) (some joint inventors available) must comply with other statutory requirements and the following: (A) all available joint inventors must make oath/declaration for themselves and on behalf of the nonsigning inventor as required by pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.175 and 1.64; (B) the application must be accompanied by proof that the nonsigning inventor cannot be found or reached after diligent effort or refuses to execute the application papers; (C) the last known address of the nonsigning joint inventor must be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An oath or declaration signed by all available joint inventors with the signature block(s) of the nonsigning inventor(s) left blank may be treated as having been signed by all available inventors on behalf of the nonsigning inventor(s), unless otherwise indicated. See MPEP § 409.03(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47(b) filing requirements (no inventor available; applicant with proprietary interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47(b) (no inventor available) is permitted only when no inventor is available and a person with demonstrated proprietary interest (including juristic entities) makes application 'on behalf of and as agent for' the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to statutory filing requirements, the 1.47(b) applicant must: (A) make the oath required by 1.63 and 1.64 (or 1.175); (B) submit proof the inventor cannot be found/reached after diligent effort or refuses to execute papers; (C) state the last known address; (D) state relationship to the inventor as required by 1.64; (E) make out a prima facie case of assignment/agreement/proprietary interest; and (F) prove that filing is necessary to preserve rights or prevent irreparable damage. See MPEP § 409.03(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of unavailability — statement of facts and documentary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When inability to find or reach a nonsigning inventor 'after diligent effort' is alleged, a statement of facts should fully describe the exact facts relied upon to establish diligent effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should be signed, where possible, by someone with firsthand knowledge; hearsay statements will not normally be accepted. Include documentary evidence such as Internet searches, certified mail return receipts, cover letters, telegrams, and the specific steps taken to locate the nonsigning inventor. The statement should contain facts, not conclusions. See MPEP § 409.03(c) and § 409.03(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required to substantiate refusal to join
rubrics_metrics.description: A refusal to join must be supported by evidence showing the inventor was properly presented with the application papers and intentionally refused to sign or accept them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send a copy of the application papers to the last known address of the nonsigning inventor or to counsel. Temporary unavailability (vacation) or hospitalization is not acceptable; pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.43 may instead be available. For alleged refusals, the circumstances must be specified in a statement of facts by a person who was present when the refusal occurred. Express written refusals (can be redacted) or evidence of a bona fide attempt to present the papers may be sufficient. See MPEP § 409.03(c)–(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of last known address
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed pursuant to pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47 must state the last known address of the nonsigning inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That address should be the last known address at which the inventor customarily receives mail (ordinarily the last known residence). Also provide other addresses where the nonsigning inventor may be reached. See MPEP § 409.03(e) and MPEP § 602.08(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie proof of proprietary interest for 1.47(b) applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47(b) applicant must make out a prima facie case that (1) the invention has been assigned to the applicant, or (2) the inventor has agreed in writing to assign the invention to the applicant, or (3) the applicant otherwise demonstrates sufficient proprietary interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assigned, submit a copy of the assignment in English and a statement under 37 CFR 3.73(b) by the assignee. An assignment solely for the purpose of obtaining a filing date is not considered an assignment under 35 U.S.C. 118 and 37 CFR 1.47(b). See MPEP § 409.03(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrating proprietary interest other than by assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Proprietary interest not obtained by assignment or agreement may be demonstrated by an appropriate legal memorandum that a court of competent jurisdiction would likely award title to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facts supporting that conclusion should be made of record by affidavit or declaration of a person with firsthand knowledge. The legal memorandum should be prepared and signed by an attorney familiar with the jurisdictional law. Submit statutes or court decisions relied upon in English. See MPEP § 409.03(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof that filing is necessary to preserve rights or prevent irreparable damage
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1.47(b) applicant must prove that filing the application is necessary (1) to preserve the rights of the parties or (2) to prevent irreparable damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irreparable damage may be established by a statement from the applicant explaining why an earlier or immediate filing date is necessary to preserve rights. See MPEP § 409.03(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for substitute statement in lieu of oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.64)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64 must comply with 1.63(a) identifying the inventor(s) and stating upon information and belief the facts the inventor would state; identify the person executing the substitute statement and their relationship to the inventor; identify the circumstances permitting execution (deceased, legal incapacity, refusal, or cannot be found after diligent effort); and, unless supplied in an ADS, identify each inventor's legal name and last known mailing address and residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute statements are available when the inventor is deceased, under legal incapacity, has refused to execute the oath/declaration, or cannot be found or reached after diligent effort. See 37 CFR 1.64 and MPEP § 604.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when a non-inventor (e.g., assignee or corporate officer) executes oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is executed by one other than the inventor (e.g., an assignee, obligated assignee, or corporate officer), the declaration must state the full name, residence, post office address, and citizenship of the nonsigning inventor; the relationship of the signer to the inventor; and, if a corporation signer, the signer's title or position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a corporation authorizes an attorney or agent to sign, submit proof of the attorney's or agent's authority (statement signed by an appropriate corporate officer) or have the attorney/agent state that they are authorized. An inventor may not authorize another individual to act as his/her agent to sign the application oath or declaration on his/her behalf. See Staeger v. Commissioner, In re Striker, and MPEP § 409.03(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and Office of Petitions handling before examiner action
rubrics_metrics.description: Application papers submitted under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47 are forwarded by OPAP to the Office of Petitions for determination whether the papers are proper, complete, and acceptable under 1.47 and for a decision on the petition before the application is sent to the Technology Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner should not mail an Office action in an application without a fully executed oath/declaration unless the application has been accorded status under 1.47 in a written decision on the petition. If a petition under 1.47 has not been decided, the application or an electronic message concerning the petition must be forwarded to the Office of Petitions. When papers are acceptable, the Office of Petitions enters a decision in the file and a notice is published in the Official Gazette. See MPEP § 409.03(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and remedies of the nonsigning inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: The nonsigning inventor (inventor designee) may protest designation as inventor, inspect papers, order copies, and make his/her position of record; may join the application by filing an appropriate oath/declaration; and may, if claiming sole inventorship, file his/her own application and request an interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nonsigning inventor is not entitled to a hearing and is not entitled to prosecute the application if status under 1.47 has been accorded or proprietary interest of the 1.47(b) applicant has been shown to the Office's satisfaction. Even if the nonsigning inventor joins, they cannot revoke or give a power of attorney without agreement of the 1.47 applicant. See MPEP § 409.03(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee/obligated assignee or person showing sufficient proprietary interest under 37 CFR 1.46 (post-September 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person to whom the inventor has assigned or is under an obligation to assign the invention, or a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest, may make an application for patent and act as applicant under 37 CFR 1.46. If filing under 35 U.S.C. 111, the application must contain an application data sheet (ADS) specifying the assignee or person showing proprietary interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant is the assignee or obligated assignee, documentary evidence of ownership (assignment, employment agreement) should be recorded in 37 CFR part 3 no later than the date the issue fee is paid (37 CFR 1.46(b)(1)). If the applicant otherwise shows proprietary interest, submit a petition including: (i) the fee in § 1.17(g), (ii) a showing of sufficient proprietary interest, and (iii) a statement that the filing by such person is appropriate to preserve rights. For international/PCT national stage or Hague design entries, the assignee/person must have been identified as applicant during the international stage. See MPEP § 409.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and publication following acceptance of a 1.47 application
rubrics_metrics.description: When papers deposited under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47 are found acceptable, the Office of Petitions enters a decision and a notice will be published in the Official Gazette identifying the application number, filing date, title of the invention, and name(s) of the nonsigning inventor(s). The USPTO will notify the nonsigning inventor(s) or, if deceased, the legal representative(s), at the last known address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may dispense with repeating the notice in a continuation or divisional if notice regarding the filing of the prior application was given. A filing date is assigned provided 37 CFR 1.53(b) requirements are met. See MPEP § 409.03(h)–(j).
